# Yata

> Yata is a free, open-source notch app for Windows 10 and 11, in the style of the Dynamic Island: a black pill at the top of the screen, just below the camera, that shows what's playing, your next meeting and your reminders, then gets out of the way. MIT license, no account, no telemetry.

Yata, also listed as Yata Notch (from Yatagarasu, the messenger crow of Japanese myth), is a desktop app for Windows written in WPF on .NET 10. Closed, the notch shows the time; hover it and it opens into tabs. It hides when an app goes full screen. A hand-drawn 16 × 14 pixel raven lives in the notch and reacts to your day.

## Features

- Now playing from any app that uses Windows media controls (Spotify, YouTube in the browser and others): cover, progress, controls and synced lyrics from LRCLIB.
- Next meeting from Google Calendar (read-only), shown in the closed notch, with a Join button for Meet, Zoom or Teams.
- Pomodoro timer (25 minutes of focus, 5 of rest, a long break every four) that pauses when you walk away.
- Daily water goal with optional nudges, and a task list where "Call Ana 15:30" becomes a reminder, with optional two-way sync to Google Tasks.
- A shelf: drop files on the notch and drag them out later. Only the path is kept.
- System indicators: volume, brightness, battery, audio output, Caps Lock, keyboard layout, network, and a dot when an app is using the microphone.
- AI coding agents: Claude Code, Cursor and Codex (Claude Code also in WSL) show in the notch while they work, when they wait for a permission or an answer, and when they're done, marked with the agent's logo and titled with the app it runs in and the project ("Orca · yata"); a click goes to the agent's window. Turned on per agent in Settings → AI agents, which adds hooks calling `yata-cli hook <agent>` to the agent's own settings (Claude Code also has a plugin). Only the state is sent, never prompts, commands or answers.
- "While you were away": notices you didn't see while away from the PC (reminders, water, battery, a paused focus session, an agent finishing) are kept, and when you're back the raven flies in with a letter listing them (on by default).
- Activities: scripts, builds and AI agents on the PC can show their progress in a bubble beside the notch with `yata-cli activity set|attention|done|fail|end` (a console tool installed next to Yata, optionally on PATH). Exit codes: 0 shown, 1 bad arguments, 2 Yata isn't running, 3 refused.
- Stays out of calls: screen sharing, recordings, OBS and screenshots do not capture the notch (on by default). Reminders held back by a full-screen app chime when they show, and come without the chime while the microphone is in use or Windows asks not to be disturbed.
- Ctrl+Alt+Y toggles the notch from anywhere. Works with multiple monitors and per-monitor scaling.

## Privacy

- Lyrics lookup sends artist, title and song length to LRCLIB (on by default, can be turned off).
- Weather sends the chosen city, rounded to about 1 km, to Open-Meteo (off by default). Never IP location.
- Google Calendar and Tasks talk directly between the PC and Google (off by default). Access is encrypted on disk with Windows DPAPI.
- Activities from other programs arrive through a local named pipe only the current Windows user can open (network refused), and stay in memory only.
- No AI: Yata uses no AI/ML model or service, and Google data is never sent to an AI provider or used to train models. Activities only flow into Yata; they cannot read events or tasks.
- No keyboard hook: Caps Lock and layout are read from key state. The diagnostic log stays on the PC for 7 days.

## Install

- Free. Windows 10 (version 2004 or later) and Windows 11, x64. About 3 MB.
- Installs per user without admin rights. If the .NET 10 Desktop Runtime is missing, the installer downloads it from Microsoft and checks Microsoft's signature before running it; that step asks for admin.
- The installer is not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen may warn on first run (More info, then Run anyway). Each release is built by GitHub Actions from the public code and ships SHA256SUMS.txt; from v0.2.1 on it also carries a GitHub build provenance attestation.
